paper_id: Li et al. - 2020 - Patronus preventing unauthorized speech recordings with support for selective unscrambling
title: Patronus: Preventing Unauthorized Speech Recordings with Support for Selective Unscrambling
motivation: Smart devices create privacy risks of secret recordings; no effective anti-recording solution exists despite real-world consequences (e.g., Ukrainian PM resignation after leaked recording).
problem_framing: Design a system achieving three properties: (1) human conversation unaffected, (2) unauthorized devices cannot clearly record, (3) authorized devices CAN record clearly.
key_insight: Exploit nonlinear effects of COTS microphones—ultrasonic signals generate low-frequency 'scramble' noise in recordings that can be canceled if the pattern is known.
method_signature: Ultrasonic scramble modulation with chirp smoothing, NLMS adaptive filtering for authorized descrambling, reflection layer for coverage.
evaluation_criteria: PESQ score, Speech Recognition Vocabulary Accuracy (SRVA), speech recognition error rates; human listening tests with 11 volunteers.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Working distance limited to <70 cm with cheap transducers; cannot perfectly handle physical attacks like placing obstacles or covering microphones.
evidence_for_taste: Patronus is the first system to leverage the nonlinear effect
